1.title: Know the words of personal wellness
1.intro: Wellness means habits that support how you feel day to day. It is not medicine and it does not replace a doctor.
pts: Learn the terms: habit, sleep, movement, nutrition, stress, goal, routine, coach.
Wellness has parts: body, mind, social and daily life.
A coach helps a person set and keep goals. A coach does not diagnose or treat illness.
Know where your role stops and a licensed health professional starts.
1.ex: A client says she is tired. A coach asks about sleep and routine, and also says: 'If tiredness lasts, please see your doctor.'
1.act: List ten wellness words with a plain meaning each and mark which ones are coaching and which are medical.
1.std: Task: define ten wellness terms and mark the coaching line. Condition: from memory, then check. Standard: all meanings plain and correct, and the line between coaching and medical care stated.

2.title: Explain how a wellness session and plan work
2.intro: A session has a shape. A plan has small steps the person can repeat.
pts: A session runs: welcome, check-in, one goal, one or two small steps, how to track, next time.
Start where the person is, not where you think they should be.
Small steps beat big promises: a ten-minute walk after lunch, a set bedtime, a glass of water with each meal.
Write the plan in the person's own words.
2.ex: Goal: 'feel less rushed in the morning.' Step one: prepare clothes and breakfast the night before, three nights this week.
2.act: Run a mock 30-minute session with a friend and write a one-page plan.
2.std: Task: run a mock session. Condition: 30 minutes with a friend. Standard: one goal, two small steps, a tracking method and a next date are written down.

3.title: Coach habits to a clear standard
3.intro: Now you apply what you know. Help a person pick a goal, track it and adjust.
pts: Make goals specific: what, how often, by when.
Ask open questions: What would make this easier? What got in the way?
Track simply: a tick on a calendar is enough.
Praise effort and progress, not weight or looks. Never promise a result.
3.ex: Before: 'Get fit.' After: 'Walk 20 minutes on Monday, Wednesday and Friday for four weeks.'
3.act: Coach one volunteer for two weeks with a weekly check-in and a simple tracker.
3.std: Task: coach one volunteer for two weeks. Condition: with consent and a written plan. Standard: goal is specific, tracker is used, no medical advice is given, and the volunteer says what helped.

4.title: Follow Canadian rules and know your limits
4.intro: Health care is regulated in each province. Wellness coaching must stay on the right side of the line.
pts: Titles such as doctor, nurse, dietitian, physiotherapist, psychotherapist and some others are protected in many provinces. Use only titles you hold; check the current rule with the local authority.
Do not diagnose, treat or promise to cure. Do not tell anyone to stop a medicine or treatment.
Advertising must be true. Do not claim miracle results.
Natural health products and supplements are regulated by the federal health agency; do not sell or advise on them unless you know the current rules and check them.
4.ex: A client asks if a herb can replace her medicine. You say that is a question for her doctor or pharmacist and offer to help her write her questions.
4.act: Make a table of what you may do, what you must refer, and who to refer to, for ten common client questions.
4.std: Task: build a scope-of-practice table. Condition: using official public pages. Standard: each row shows a referral or a safe coaching reply and a source; no guesswork.

5.title: Price your sessions and check it pays
5.intro: You earn only what remains after costs and unbilled time.
pts: Time includes prep, session, notes, travel and admin.
Hourly cost = yearly costs plus the pay you need, divided by hours you can really bill.
Compare single sessions, packages and group sessions.
Sales tax may apply to some services; check the small-supplier limit with the tax agency.
5.ex: A 60-minute session takes 90 minutes with prep and notes. At 60 USD per session, that is 40 USD per hour of real time. Teaching figures only.
5.act: Time three sessions end to end and set a price for each format.
5.std: Task: price three formats. Condition: from your own time log. Standard: hours, price and result shown and a mentor can follow every number.

6.title: Find clients and show proof
6.intro: People choose a coach they trust. Show your method and your care.
pts: Write a one-page description of who you help and how, in plain words and without health claims.
Offer a free 20-minute chat so people can meet you.
Ask permission before using any client story, and remove names.
Keep a simple list: contact, date, reply, next step. Only contact people who agree to hear from you.
6.ex: A post says: 'I help busy parents build a simple evening routine.' It makes no claim about health outcomes.
6.act: Hold five intro chats and log the results.
6.std: Task: run five intro chats. Condition: with consent and no pressure. Standard: notes kept, no claims made, and one lesson written.

7.title: Protect privacy, safety and quality
7.intro: Clients share personal things. Keep them safe.
pts: Health and personal details are sensitive. Keep notes locked and share nothing without written consent.
Know when to refer: signs of serious illness, self-harm, abuse or an eating disorder. Have a list of local services ready.
Keep a short written agreement: services, fees, cancellation, privacy and your limits.
Consider insurance for your work; ask an adviser.
7.ex: Your agreement says: 'I am a coach, not a health care provider. I do not diagnose or treat. I will refer you when a matter is outside my role.'
7.act: Write an agreement template and a referral list for your area.
7.std: Task: produce an agreement and a referral list. Condition: reviewed by a mentor. Standard: scope, fees, privacy and limits are all in plain words.

8.title: Run a coaching practice for 60 days
8.intro: Now you run it for real, measure and decide.
pts: Set a goal such as three clients and ten sessions.
Each week record hours, income, client progress and what you learned.
Ask each client for feedback and one improvement.
Choose at the end: stop, change or grow, and write a 12-month plan.
8.ex: After 60 days: 3 clients, 10 sessions, 600 USD, two clients returned. You decide to offer a four-week package.
8.act: Run the pilot and present a 12-month plan to a panel of three.
8.std: Task: run a 60-day pilot. Condition: real clients and a signed agreement. Standard: log complete, no medical claims made, and the plan uses numbers.

quiz: What is the difference between coaching and medical care?
A coach helps with habits and goals; a doctor diagnoses and treats.
What is a good goal?
Specific: what, how often and by when.
What should you never promise?
A cure or a guaranteed result.
What do you do if a client asks about stopping medicine?
Refer them to their doctor or pharmacist.
Why use only titles you hold?
Many health titles are protected by provincial law.
How do you track a habit simply?
A tick on a calendar.
What does an agreement list?
Services, fees, cancellation, privacy and limits.
When must you refer a client?
When the matter is medical or serious and outside your role.
Why get consent before using a story?
Client information is private.
What do you do when you do not know a rule?
Check the current rule with the local authority.
